utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-94-2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We're very grateful to the technical area and to the court reporter for managing to redo whatever they have to do so that we can start as soon as possible after the previous hearing. Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If it please the Court. Dirk Ryneveld and Daryl Mundis for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Eugene O'Sullivan appearing on behalf of Mr. Nikolic. Your Honour, with your leave, can we be allowed to have our interpreter, Ms. Mirkavic, present in the courtroom, should the need arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. This is a Status Conference in accordance with Rule 65 bis -- First of all, I should ask: Mr. Nikolic, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, are there any matters in accordance with the terms of the Rule that you wish to raise at this stage, that is, in relation to your client's well-being?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In that regard, Your Honour, I met with my client prior to this hearing and he is experiencing some dental problems which are being attended to in the Detention Unit. However, he informs me that the problems affect his lower jaw and teeth, and, in effect, when he tries to eat, it causes him discomfort, and he is anxious to ensure that he receives the proper dental attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But you say they are being attended to.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It's being attended to by a nurse who relays her findings to a dentist. He has yet not seen a dentist and he is hopeful that if the problem persists that he will, in fact, be visited by a dentist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: My suggestion, as the first step to be taken, is to put in a report to the commander or the commandant out at the Detention Unit. That usually has some effect. If there is no action taken, then your client should contact the Registrar who refers those matters to the President. But hopefully he will get the dental treatment that he needs, and as soon as it is possible. I rather suspect that the inmates of the Detention Unit get faster dental treatment than most citizens who live in the Netherlands, from my own experience anyway. Thank you. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Nothing else, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in relation to the documents that we seem to run into every time, Mr. Ryneveld, what is happening with the compliance with Rule 66(A)(i)?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With respect to 66(A)(i), we have provided, by consent with Defence counsel, Mr. Morrison, the, shall we say, pre-Brdjanin disclosure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean everything's been redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: It has. Unfortunately that is the situation we find ourselves in. But rather than wait to provide him with materials while we are making contact with some 38 or more witnesses to find whether or not the specifics of the protective measures that we will eventually have to make an application before the Court, we thought -- and at the Defence's request, we have provided them redacted materials in their entirety. We appreciate the fact that the Brdjanin decision requires us to make specific requests for protective measures with details. We are unable at this time to make such a request because each of those 38 people have to be contacted and details formulated. That is the situation we're in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, that wasn't required by the Brdjanin decision, that's required by the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It was simply that the Prosecution turned a blind eye to what the Rules said and adopted its own protective measures scheme which had not been approved by anybody. I noticed, by the way, in a note between counsel with which we've been supplied that the Prosecution claims to have relied upon an earlier protective order issued by the Trial Chamber which was a surprise to me. Perhaps you could identify what protective measures order was issued by the Trial Chamber upon which some reliance is purported to have been placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Perhaps Your Honour could indicate to me what correspondence or the date of the correspondence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, it's a letter from Dermot Groome, legal officer, to Mr. Morrison --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- recording terms of a conversation, and it says: "I informed you that redactions were made to the discovery material pursuant to an earlier protective order issued by the Trial Chamber, as well as the general practice before Brdjanin." That may have been an excess of enthusiasm on Mr. Groome's part, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm unable to make an informed response to that. I'm certainly not aware personally of any previous order. It may have been that following our previous practice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that I can understand, and one hopes that it's now been stopped, that previous practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But nevertheless I was curious to know what the earlier protective order was upon which Mr. Groome relied.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm unable to assist you on that particular issue, but I will certainly check our file and provide the Court with a copy if one, indeed, is located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There may be one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm not saying there isn't; I'm just not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, what sort of time frame are we talking about for compliance with 66(A)(ii), the copies of the statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I understand that it could take us, especially with the August recess and matters of that nature, that we could probably comply with that by the end of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, this trial won't start this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So we're in plenty of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm just wondering whether somebody had given any consideration to a time limit yet, because I think we should try and keep it under some form of control.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Absolutely. If I know my learned friend, he is as anxious as we are to get together to make the necessary stipulations, to shorten the matters. As you can see, the whole purpose of what we've done so far is to provide him with as much information as possible, because there were three volumes of material which they can start to look at while they're waiting for the redacted names. My friends have been quite understanding that we want to have the appropriate time to make the application for protective witnesses, because to provide it in advance would render the whole process moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. What should we do about the motion for protective measures in pre-Brdjanin style which is presently in the file?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: My suggestion is that we agree that it is suspended or withdrawn until you seek to have it reinstated in, hopefully, some amended form.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I had interpreted the order, which referred to a pending decision in Brdjanin, as actually relating to our case, so I assumed that the Brdjanin-type order would also affect us. If I recall correctly, we were given seven days within which to make a further motion, which we have not had an opportunity to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy to give you extra time to do so, but I think we should -- I don't like motions just sitting in the list. Somebody at some stage is going to go through these files and say, "This Trial Chamber failed even to deal with a motion in accordance with the Rules." I'm happy to extend it or to suspend it so that you can replace it or something like that, but I think we should have some sort of time limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Might I ask for an extension until the end of September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: -- by way of a suspension, perhaps, and we fully intend to bring on a replacement application with particulars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Have you any problem with that, Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The consequence of this, of course, is that you haven't yet complied with 66(A)(i), so that if we can have an informal agreement that time, under Rule 72, for preliminary motions doesn't start to run until you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Counsel have, in fact, discussed that very issue, and I think my friend wanted to ensure that that issue got on the record; that until such time as we have filed some notice of compliance in accordance, then time doesn't start to run.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There's always trouble here because some counsel for the accused, if they come from the former Yugoslavia particularly, want to have a suspension of the time running under Rule 72 until they get all the material in B/C/S. But that doesn't seem to be the situation here because we have either Mr. Morrison or Mr. O'Sullivan who can read the material in the state it is now. But there will be a time, I suppose, when the Defence will say the accused has to be able to read this material as well. From the point of view of Rule 72, we'll wait and see what happens in relation to your compliance with Rule 66 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I've just been assured that all the materials have, in fact, been translated into B/C/S, so that is not a problem for us in this instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It seems to be a continuing one, but I'm glad to see that it doesn't arise here. I raise, only because I always raise, the question of Rule 68 and exculpatory material.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I can assure the Court that we are aware of our ongoing obligations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: -- and that we are, as we are going through these materials, disclosing Rule 68 material as and when it's discovered. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You do understand that it was not a personal matter in the previous case with Krnojelac, but there have been so many complaints that we thought that something had to be done, and perhaps it's had some salutary effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: One might hope. I can only say that as far as I know in the Kunarac case, which Your Honour has been conducting, we haven't had any of those difficulties arising. So hopefully --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's been remarkable and very good. Now, is there anything else you want to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Not that I can think of at the moment. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, it may have been resolved informally, but we have had a number of problems raising your lead counsel, Mr. Morrison. He has committed the fatal sin, so far as we can find out, of not only telling his secretary where he is, but he has failed to tell his clerk where he is. And for a barrister not to tell his clerk where he may be would probably be the worst possible thing he could do. We were told he is somewhere in Africa but they didn't know where. He's made a complaint, and perhaps it is a justifiable one, that he only got 14 days' notice of the hearing today. If we can contact him to find out when it would be convenient for him to be here, we would be in a better position. But it seemed that anything that we sent to his Chambers would not get to him because they didn't know when he was going to get back. So I understand he has disclosed his e-mail address; I hope it's one that he can access from places other than the United Kingdom. That may be the answer. But we want to be in a position to be able to contact him rather than just leave things for him to read when he finally gets back to the UK. So would you emphasise to him when you're speaking to him that we really do want to obtain from him his availability before we fix dates but we were unable to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'll ensure that he's made aware of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is there anything else that you want to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much for standing in, Mr. O'Sullivan. That is all. We shall adjourn.
